## Summary (Ask Bunkankun 聞分館君)

This 6-fascicle work by the great Qīng Buddhist scholar [續法](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E7%BA%8C%E6%B3%95) Xùfǎ (1641–1728) is the most ambitious early-Qīng commentary on [法藏](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E6%B3%95%E8%97%8F) Fǎzàng's *Five Teachings* doxography (cf. *[Wǔ jiào zhāng](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6e/KR6e0074)*). Xùfǎ — known in the East Asian Buddhist tradition as one of the most important late-imperial Huáyán-school authorities — restructures Fǎzàng's classical schema in a *yí* 儀 ("ritual procedures") format, providing systematic instruction for monastic-doctrinal study.

**Abstract**

The bracket adopted here (1660 – 1715) reflects [續法](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E7%BA%8C%E6%B3%95) Xùfǎ's mature scholarly activity. The *Wǔ jiào yí* is part of Xùfǎ's vast commentary corpus on the Huáyán-school doctrinal apparatus, which together (cf. *[Wǔ jiào yí kāi méng](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6e/KR6e0143)*, *[Duàn zhèng sān jué jiǎn làn tú](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6e/KR6e0144)*, etc.) constitutes the late-imperial Huáyán doctrinal curriculum.

The work is preserved in the Manji *Xù zàng jīng* (X1024) collection.
